# ChoreScore product reconstruction — operating mission

The owner wants the application completed, not an audit, a CI dashboard or an
APK factory. Work directly in feat/product-reconstruction, integrated PR #2.
All work must remain free. The latest explicit owner instruction authorizes
one OpenCode worker to audit, implement and iterate using the earlier projects.

OpenCode's remote free endpoint actually refused every tested model with
"Free usage limit reached" on 2 November. Do not pay, change identities, rotate
IPs or bypass that limit. The worker now runs Apache-2.0 Qwen3 weights on the
standard public GitHub runner CPU through localhost llama.cpp. No inference
API key, provider account, GPU or billing service is involved. Model and runtime
revisions/checksums are recorded. The nonce probe must prove real inference.

Read AGENTS.md, CODEX_MISSION.md, PRODUCT.md and the cumulative requirements
matrix in docs/CROSS_REPOSITORY_REQUIREMENTS.md. The originals are pinned by
docs/source-history/manifest.json: consult the original section relevant to
the chosen repair. Read .opencode-ci/latest-checks.md FIRST. Choose ONE concrete
failing behavior, read its source/tests, edit it directly and run its test.
Do not reread the complete historical VERIFICATION.md or all 34 snapshots on
every pass; use the current matrix and relevant original requirement. Never
call task, invent session identifiers or delegate implementation to explore.
Use V1's visual quality and retained V2/V3 privacy requirements. Do not bring
back the abandoned chrono, ranking, paywall, premium or public demo.

At each pass:
1. Audit the actual current source and the first concrete failing check.
2. Repair that failure. If checks pass, implement the next incomplete vertical
   product slice from the requirements matrix, including persistence/errors/UI.
3. Add a meaningful regression test. Existing tests and specifications are
   protected by the harness; do not edit or bypass them.
4. Verify exact accounting, group isolation, identity permanence, atomic todos,
   private media and offline recovery. Never replace real services by mocks.
5. Record what changed and what was really executed in VERIFICATION.md.

Priority: official Firestore authority and direct-client attacks, complete
native photo/reminder/share/todo journeys, real collaboration, then remaining
UX/accessibility and persistent consent-based research. Do not claim in-memory
transport tests prove Firestore rules or an iOS JS export proves an iPhone run.
No Firebase production access is provided to this worker. Do not enable billing,
create production users, send messages, or invent credentials. If an external
step cannot be performed, continue independent product work and state the gap.

Do not modify .github/, scripts/ci/, opencode.json, the mission documents,
historical snapshots or existing tests. Do not change Git history, commit,
push, merge, dispatch workflows or use a paid model. The trusted runner handles
verification and publication. A prose-only update is rejected. Do not weaken
security, suppress app crashes/ANRs or skip the real native assertions.

No claim of "perfect" or "complete" is accepted without the actual native,
cross-account Firebase, privacy, accounting and UI acceptance evidence. Green
automated checks establish their covered scenarios only.

Verified source is integrated by the trusted publisher, which explicitly
resumes the same programme on that new revision. Existing public GitHub token
push suppression must never silently stop product reconstruction. If an
external service cannot run or no verified patch is produced, the failed
checks and candidates remain evidence; do not publish a false completion.
